text: Your Wi-Fi card understands that there is an access point called Ngimouse, and it will also measure the associated SNR. That means how strong that signal can be received. Okay, and then it just waits there and wait to see if there is any other beacon from another access point. And if there is, it will record it, and it will record also the associated SNR, and so on. After a while, it switches to another frequency channel, in this case the second one, and it will stay there, waiting to receive possible beacons from the nearby access points. And it will record the name of the access point and the associated SNR. So how strong the signal from that access point can be received. You will stay there for a while and then switch to the third frequency channel. Okay, so if your Wi-Fi card also works at 5 gigahertz, it will then switch to 5 gigahertz, scan all the frequency channels at 5 gigahertz, and on each of them, it will hear for beacons, record the name of the access point, sending that beacon and the associated SNR, and so on and so forth. So at the end of this scanning procedure, what your Wi-Fi.
